subject: Re: Incident notification — proposed timeline, subprocessor access, and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-secops@acmehealth.com, sam.murphy@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA — incident notification language and subprocessor involvement

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier this week. Our legal team has one outstanding ask on the DPA related to incident notification and subprocessor cooperation before we can push the redline to procurement. Attached is our proposed language (ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf). High-level asks:

- Initial notification within 48 hours of becoming aware for incidents impacting Acme customer data (with an expectation of material detail).
- Preservation of high-fidelity logs and a snapshot for forensic analysis for 90 days; access by a third-party forensic vendor if needed.
- Explicit commitment to notify us of any subprocessor involvement in an incident within 48 hours and to coordinate direct handoff to the subprocessor where evidence resides.
- Cross-border evidence transfer: we need an assurance that forensic exports will be handled under standard SCCs or equivalent and that data will be minimized/pseudonymized where possible.

Please confirm Redwood's position on each item and any operational limitations we should be aware of. If you prefer, we can mark up your standard incident clause rather than exchanging language in prose.

Best,
Priya Sethi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Health

(Attachment: ACME_DPA_redline_v3.pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification language and subprocessor involvement

Priya — thanks, we received the redline. Looping in Ben (security liaison) and Kim (contracts) to scope operational feasibility. Quick read and proposed compromise below; Ben/Kim please weigh in.

High-level proposal from Redwood:
- Initial notification: 72 hours after confirmation of a security incident materially affecting Acme customer data. We can provide a preliminary summary sooner (within 48 hours) if there is certainty on impact, but we need the 72-hour window for validated details.
- Evidence & logs: we retain high-fidelity requestable snapshots for 14 days and can provide targeted forensic exports (timeboxed) for up to 90 days on request. Full 90-day live retention is possible with a scoped collection request and export approval.
- Subprocessor involvement: Redwood will notify Acme of any subprocessor implicated in an incident within 5 business days of identification and will coordinate an evidence handoff if the evidence resides with that subprocessor.
- Cross-border exports: we will comply with SCCs or equivalent legal basis for transfers. For forensic exports we recommend pseudonymization where it preserves investigative value. Any export to a jurisdiction with greater legal risk will require prior notice and a written export plan.

Operational asks from Redwood:
- If Acme intends to deploy a third‑party forensic vendor, please confirm the vendor and we will provide a secure read-only snapshot path; vendor access will require an executed N NDA (we can provide a Redwood-forensics NDA template) and a scoped data request.
- For timeboxed high-fidelity snapshots, we need precise time ranges and selectors (e.g., session ids, trace ids) to limit the export. Broad requests force manual sifting and extend timelines.

Attachments: I attached our MAP template we use for incident coordination. If Acme is happy with the 72 hour initial+48 hour preliminary wording and the scoped 90-day export approach, we can put those lines into your redline and return a countersigned DPA for procurement.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm retention and typical extraction turnaround? Kim, I think we should propose specific redline wording for the 72/90/5bd compromise.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redwood_MAP_template.docx)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification language and subprocessor involvement

Marissa — quick technical notes for the reply to Acme:

- Retention: we keep full request/response traces and per-request telemetry for 14 days with high resolution (request headers, body hashes, routing metadata). Aggregated token-level metrics and billing traces are retained for 90 days.
- For forensic exports: our standard workflow is a scoped snapshot (S3 export) that includes logs, request traces and any relevant binary artifacts; typical turnaround for a scoped export is 3-7 business days from receipt of a precise selector. If selectors are vague we need 10+ business days.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a live subprocessors roster; most are US/EU-based (hosting, monitoring, observability, and a single analytics vendor in APAC). We will not use subprocessors in sanction-risk jurisdictions. We will provide the current roster and notify if a subprocessor is implicated.
- Access model: vendor access is via a timebound export location or a remote read-only viewer run by Redwood staff. Direct account-level access is not granted.

Operational caveat: if Acme requires immutable forensic snapshots retained by Acme or the vendor for 90+ days under Redwood control, that constitutes a special evidence escrow and will need an SOW with associated costs and export approvals.

I can provide the subprocessors list and our standard forensic NDA to Priya.

Ben
Ben Carter
Security Liaison, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-secops@acmehealth.com, forensics@forenex.com
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification language and subprocessor involvement

Marissa/Ben — thanks for the detailed reply and the compromise language. Acme can accept the 72-hour validated-notification coupled with a best-effort 48-hour preliminary alert; that addresses our procurement risk.

We will:
- Provide Forenex as our preferred vendor and execute Redwood's forensic NDA. Forenex can work with selectors you provide.
- Accept scoped exports rather than full 90-day live retention — the scoped S3 export workflow is fine.
- Please send the current subprocessors roster and flag if any are located outside the EU/US. If there are contractual constraints we will surface them quickly.

Next: please produce a single-page DPA supplement with the agreed bullet points so we can attach it to our procurement packet. Also share the DocuSign link when ready and the MAP drive folder for the incident coordination plan.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Priya Sethi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Health
